title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page continues the study of the 'loop equation' (32)/(49), [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε1(μ^{-1}), in G ≅ GL(2) over a variable base. α = (a b; c d) and β = (r s; t u) are variable sections. ρ = (0 v1; v w) and σ = (0 v1'; v' w') are fixed elements, linked by relations (52), and [x,y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}. On the previous page Grothendieck computed ξ = [α,ρ] = (A B; C D). He found (-δ_α v v1)B = -v v1 bd + v1² ac + v1 w bc and (-δ_α v v1)D = -v v1 d² + v1 w cd + v1² c². He also showed that a right-hand side of the form y·ε1-type triangular factor forces u = (1/U S/U; 0 1), i.e. μ = 1/U and λ = S/U.

This page:
(55) The same computation for y = [β,σ] = (R S; T U) gives (-v v1 δ_β)S = ±(v1 v)su + v1² tr - v1 w' st and (-v v1 δ_β)U = -(v1 v)u² - v1 w' tu + v1² t². These are just (54) with a,b,c,d → r,s,t,u and the substitutions (52). He notes that one may divide by v1.
(56) Dividing by v1 gives D = (-v d² + w cd + v1 c²)/(-v(ad-bc)) and μ = 1/D. Then B/D = (-v bd + v1 ac + w bc)/(-v d² + w cd + v1 c²) = λ. So the triangular element u = (μ λ; 0 1) is expressed explicitly in terms of the bottom/top rows of α and the parameters of ρ.
(57) For v1 = 1 the numerator is c² + w cd - v d² = det(dρ + c·I), and the denominator -vδ_α = det ρ · det α. Hence D(α) = det(dρ + c)/(det ρ det α).
(58) Therefore D(α) is invertible ⇔ dρ + c·I is invertible.
The page breaks off with 'mais je m'aperçois que c'est une forme produit'. He seems to notice that the numerator is a norm/product form: det(dρ + c) = (c + dθ1)(c + dθ2) over the eigenvalues θi of ρ, i.e. a norm from the algebra Z[ρ]. Equivalently, it is the binary quadratic form v x² + w xy - v1 y² (evaluated at (d,c), up to sign), which cuts out the fixed points of the Möbius transformation of ρ. Evaluating at the bottom row (c,d) of α measures whether α^{-1}(∞) is a fixed point of ρ.

Purpose. Solving the loop equation in GL(2)/PGL(2) requires parametrising μ in terms of α. The next page passes to PGL(2) (= Aut(G)) and to the condition Tr σ = 0.
errors: In (55) the first term of the S-formula is written +(v1 v)su. Obtaining it from the B-formula of (54) by a→r, b→s, c→t, d→u and v'=-v, v1'=-v1 gives -(v1 v)su, by analogy with the U-formula, where the sign is correct. This is a probable sign slip, unless it is a transcription/reading issue.

Formula (57) holds only for v1 = 1, as Grothendieck states. For general v1, det(dρ + c) = c² + cdw - v v1 d², which is not proportional to the numerator v1c² + wcd - vd². The correct general statement is homogeneous in the parameters of ρ (one should use ρ scaled appropriately).

ideas.what: Explicit computation of the commutator [α,ρ] in GL(2) and extraction of the (B,D) entries to solve [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·(upper triangular)
ideas.modern_name: commutator computations in GL2 / solving word equations in SL2

ideas.what: D(α) = det(dρ + c)/(det ρ det α): the relevant entry is a norm form (binary quadratic form attached to ρ) evaluated at the bottom row of α; invertibility criterion (58)
ideas.modern_name: norm form / fixed-point quadratic form of a Möbius transformation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gauss–Klein; binary quadratic forms attached to SL2 elements)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit 2x2 matrix algebra in service of the 'équation des lacets' notes. The determinant/norm-form observation is classical and elementary, and the thread is immediately redirected on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The first line is a short heading of the form 'et on trouve de même' (not 'de [?] ='). The context is the analogous computation for [β,σ].
The image writes y = (β,σ) (the commutator [β,σ]), not (ρ,σ).

In (56)-(57) the image shows struck-over factors: the original had v v1 etc. and v1² c², with v1 then crossed out/divided. The clean version D = (-v d² + w cd + v1 c²)/(-v(ad-bc)) is the intended one.
'(et des paramètres u, v, w qui déterminent ρ)' should read v1, v, w.
The line 'la condition de "D inv."' is struck out in the manuscript.
